chunks: Safwan narrated from Ishaq ibn Ammar who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who performed Tawaf around the Ka'bah, then went out and performed Sa'y between Safa and Marwah. While he was performing Sa'y, he remembered that he had left part of his Tawaf around the House incomplete. He (the Imam) said: 'He should be done) said: 'He should return to the House and complete his Tawaf, then return to Safa and Marwah and complete what remains.' I said: 'What if he began with Safa and Marwah before beginning with the House?' He said: 'He should go to the House, perform Tawaf around it, then restart his Tawaf between Safa and Marwah.' I said: 'What is the difference between these two cases?' He said: 'Because in this case he had entered into part of the Tawaf, and in this case he had not entered into any part of it.'

key_terms.صَفَا: Safa (one of the hills between which Sa'y is performed)
key_terms.ٱلْبَيْت: Al-Bayt (The House, referring to the Ka'bah)
key_terms.ٱلْمَرْوَةِ: Marwah (the second hill in the Sa'y ritual)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference in ruling when a pilgrim starts Sa'y before Tawaf versus starting Tawaf before Sa'y?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), highlighting the juristic distinction between 'incomplete completion' (where the pilgrim resumes the interrupted act) and 'renewal' (where the act is restarted from the beginning) based on the point of interruption. This distinction underscores the Shia emphasis on the continuity of ritual intent (niyyah) and the physical state of the worshipper, ensuring that minor errors in sequence do not invalidate the entire pillar of Hajj. The ruling reflects the practical legal methodology (usul al-fiqh) of the Ahl al-Bayt, prioritizing ease for the pilgrim while maintaining ritual integrity.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2824 - Safwan narrated from Ishaq ibn Ammar:

I asked Abu Abdullah (as) about a man who performed Tawaf around the Ka'bah and then went out to perform Sa’y between Safa and Marwah. While he was performing Sa’y, he remembered that he had left part of his Tawaf incomplete.
Abu Abdullah (as) replied: "He should return to the Ka'bah, complete his Tawaf, and then return to Safa and Marwah to finish the remaining Sa’y."
I further asked: "What if he began with Safa and Marwah before performing Tawaf around the Ka'bah?"
Imam (as) replied: "He should go to the Ka'bah, perform Tawaf, and then restart his Sa’y between Safa and Marwah."
I then inquired: "What is the difference between these two cases?"
Imam (as) replied: "In the first case, he had already entered into part of the Tawaf, whereas in the second case, he had not yet begun any part of it."
